advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the 'static vs moving' reason so it only claims 'stalled' when >=2 samples were actually taken (e.g. treat len(github_shas) < 2 as 'insufficient samples to classify' rather than 'static').
evidence: src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:230: `verdict["reason"] = (` ... `"GitHub tip static across {len(github_shas)} samples — replication stalled"`

With attempts=1 the loop runs once (range(1, max(1,1)+1)); on divergence github_shas has exactly one element so set() has size 1 and the 'stalled' branch is always chosen — staticness was never observed across time.
advisory.finding: In the all-diverged branch the 'static vs moving' distinction is computed as `len(set(github_shas)) == 1`, which is trivially true when only one sample was taken (attempts<=1, or the clamped-to-1 case). The verdict then claims 'GitHub tip static across 1 samples — replication stalled' although the code never re-sampled and cannot know the tip is static — a static-vs-moving verdict derived from a single observation.
scenarios: Operator runs `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication --lag-attempts 1` during divergence and gets a 'replication stalled' reason that was never actually measured.
A single-sample invocation misattributes GitHub-ahead/foreign divergence as 'stalled'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Only emit the 'static — replication stalled' reason when `len(github_shas) >= 2`; for a single sample use a neutral 'diverged (single sample, no re-sample window)' reason.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject `--lag-attempts < 1` (and negative `--lag-delay`) at argument-parse time instead of silently clamping.
evidence: src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:213: `for sample in range(1, max(1, attempts) + 1):`
src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:290: `--lag-attempts` argparse entry with `type=int` and no `choices`/validation
A value of 0 or -5 is accepted by argparse and clamped to 1 silently.
advisory.finding: `--lag-attempts` accepts 0 or negative integers with no validation; the wrapper silently clamps via `max(1, attempts)` so those values run exactly one sample. The user's intent (e.g. disable/repeat count) is silently altered rather than rejected.
scenarios: Operator passes `--lag-attempts 0` expecting to skip re-sampling and instead gets a single-sample run with a possibly-misleading 'stalled' reason.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert verdicts[0]['reason'] contains 'moving but never converged' (and samples==3) in test_persistent_divergence_moving_github_tip_stays_loud.
evidence: src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:233-236: else branch sets reason='GitHub tip moving but never converged with Gerrit across {n} samples'
tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py:252-255: seq = _ShaSequence([("new","a"),("new","b"),("new","c")]) ... assert code==1; assert verdicts[0]["healthy"] is False
Named violating input: pairs [(new,a),(new,b),(new,c)] exercises the else branch, but no assertion on verdicts[0]['reason'] distinguishes it from the 'stalled' branch.
advisory.finding: The newly-added 'moving but never converged' reason branch (the else at lines 233-236) is not asserted by any test. test_persistent_divergence_moving_github_tip_stays_loud only asserts exit code 1 and healthy is False, which is identical to what the static-tip branch would report; the distinguishing reason string is never checked, so a bug swapping the 'stalled' vs 'moving but never converged' branches (or an incorrect samples count in the else path) would not be caught.
scenarios: A regression that routes moving-tip divergence into the 'stalled' reason string, or miscounts samples in the else path, ships undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert "moving but never converged" in verdicts[0]["reason"]` and `assert verdicts[0]["samples"] == 3` to the moving-tip test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs the persistent-divergence path with a custom lag_delay_seconds and asserts seq.sleeps == [delay, delay], plus a main()-level test exercising --lag-attempts/--lag-delay.
evidence: src/rebar/mirror_guard.py adds parser.add_argument('--lag-attempts', ...) and '--lag-delay', ... and passes lag_attempts=args.lag_attempts, lag_delay_seconds=args.lag_delay into run()
tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py:207,217-218,263,272: seq.sleeps recorded but only asserted == [] (never asserts the delay value or count in the divergence tests)
ABSENCE: no test invokes mirror_guard.main() with argv containing --lag-attempts/--lag-delay, so the arg->run() plumbing added in this diff is unexercised.
advisory.finding: The new --lag-attempts and --lag-delay CLI arguments and their propagation through main() into run()/_replication_check_with_lag_tolerance are untested, and no test asserts the actual delay value handed to _sleep. The _ShaSequence.sleeps list records delays but only emptiness is ever checked; a bug wiring --lag-delay to the wrong parameter, or defaulting to a wrong value, would pass.
scenarios: A future edit mis-binds --lag-delay to lag_attempts (or vice versa), or the default 45.0/3 drifts; the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In a persistent-divergence test pass lag_delay_seconds=7.0 and assert seq.sleeps == [7.0, 7.0]; add a main()/argv test asserting the flags reach run().
